questions.stem: A secreted factor acts on the same cell that released it. What is the mode?
questions.why: Autocrine signalling targets the secreting cell itself.

questions.stem: A mediator diffuses to a neighbouring cell through interstitial fluid. What type of signalling is involved?
questions.why: Paracrine mediators act locally without travelling through the circulation.

questions.stem: Which hormone is transported in plasma mainly without a protein carrier?
questions.why: Water-soluble catecholamines circulate largely unbound.

questions.stem: An acute increase in thyroid-binding globulin first increases which hormone pool?
questions.why: Additional binding sites initially bind more T4; feedback later restores free hormone.

questions.stem: Which hormone activates a cell-surface receptor with a second-messenger cascade?
questions.why: Glucagon is a peptide and binds a membrane G-protein-coupled receptor.

questions.stem: Defective intracellular glucocorticoid receptors primarily impair which process?
questions.why: Cortisol-bound intracellular receptors regulate gene transcription.

questions.stem: A fall in plasma calcium directly raises PTH without pituitary stimulation. Which control is this?
questions.why: Changes in plasma mineral concentration can directly control endocrine secretion.

questions.stem: Why is a random GH sample often a poor measure of total secretion?
questions.why: Growth hormone secretion is pulsatile and varies with sleep and other stimuli.

questions.stem: Damage to hypothalamic portal vessels most directly reduces regulation of which secretion?
questions.why: Anterior pituitary cells receive hypothalamic releasing factors through portal blood.

questions.stem: Which structure synthesizes vasopressin before its storage in the posterior pituitary?
questions.why: Supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei synthesize posterior pituitary hormones.

questions.stem: Damage to the pituitary stalk prevents normal delivery of dopamine. Which hormone tends to rise?
questions.why: Dopamine provides tonic hypothalamic inhibition of prolactin secretion.

questions.stem: Which signal stimulates ADH release during simple water deprivation?
questions.why: Hypothalamic osmoreceptors respond to elevated plasma tonicity.

questions.stem: Severe blood loss increases ADH without an initial change in osmolarity. What signal is responsible?
questions.why: Low effective circulating volume provides nonosmotic stimulation of ADH.

questions.stem: A patient with persistent ADH excess retains water. Which result is expected?
questions.why: Disproportionate water retention causes dilutional hyponatraemia and hypotonicity.

questions.stem: Polyuria remains severe after desmopressin is given. Which defect best explains the observation?
questions.why: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus is caused by renal insensitivity to vasopressin.

questions.stem: During suckling, which cells contract to expel milk already formed in alveoli?
questions.why: Oxytocin contracts myoepithelial cells and drives the milk ejection reflex.

questions.stem: Cervical stretch causes oxytocin release, stronger contractions and more stretch. What loop is this?
questions.why: Oxytocin promotes further cervical stretch and reinforces its own stimulus.

questions.stem: What mediator accounts for much GH-driven growth of epiphyseal cartilage?
questions.why: IGF-1 transmits major growth-promoting effects of GH.

questions.stem: A child has normal GH but markedly reduced hepatic IGF-1. Which response is most impaired?
questions.why: Linear skeletal growth depends substantially on GH-stimulated IGF-1.

questions.stem: Which factor suppresses rather than stimulates normal GH release?
questions.why: High blood glucose tends to suppress GH secretion.

questions.stem: Why does chronic GH excess enlarge hands and jaw but not height in adults?
questions.why: Plate fusion prevents further longitudinal growth, although appositional growth continues.

questions.stem: A prolactinoma can cause amenorrhoea through which mechanism?
questions.why: Elevated prolactin suppresses GnRH and thus gonadotropin secretion.

questions.stem: Why does copious milk secretion begin after delivery despite high prolactin in pregnancy?
questions.why: The fall in progesterone removes inhibition of full lactogenesis.

questions.stem: In primary adrenal failure, excess ACTH and skin pigmentation share which precursor?
questions.why: POMC is processed into ACTH and melanocortin-related peptides.

questions.stem: Which transporter brings iodide into thyroid follicular cells against its gradient?
questions.why: The sodium-iodide symporter concentrates iodide using the sodium gradient.

questions.stem: Which reactions in the colloid depend on thyroid peroxidase?
questions.why: Thyroid peroxidase oxidizes and organifies iodine and catalyses iodotyrosine coupling.

questions.stem: Coupling two diiodotyrosine residues produces which thyroid hormone?
questions.why: DIT plus DIT yields thyroxine, or T4.

questions.stem: A thionamide inhibits thyroid peroxidase. Which process is reduced most directly?
questions.why: Organification and coupling required for new hormone synthesis are blocked.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes thyroid hormone storage from most endocrine storage?
questions.why: Large stores of iodinated thyroglobulin accumulate in follicular colloid.

questions.stem: TSH promotes T3 and T4 release from stored colloid mainly by what mechanism?
questions.why: Colloid is endocytosed and thyroglobulin is proteolysed to liberate hormones.

questions.stem: Why is T3 more biologically potent than T4 at many target cells?
questions.why: T3 binds and activates thyroid hormone receptors more effectively.

questions.stem: Which enzymes convert much circulating T4 into active T3 in peripheral tissues?
questions.why: Deiodinases remove one iodine atom from T4 to generate T3.

questions.stem: High resting oxygen consumption in thyrotoxicosis indicates increased what?
questions.why: Thyroid hormone is calorigenic and increases basal metabolic rate.

questions.stem: Thyroid hormone can lower LDL cholesterol mainly by increasing what?
questions.why: Upregulated hepatic LDL receptors enhance clearance of circulating LDL.

questions.stem: What contributes to tachycardia in a patient with thyroid hormone excess?
questions.why: Thyroid hormone increases cardiac responsiveness to catecholamines.

questions.stem: Why can peripheral resistance fall while cardiac output increases in hyperthyroidism?
questions.why: Extra heat generation promotes peripheral vasodilatation.

questions.stem: Delayed ankle-jerk relaxation classically suggests which endocrine disturbance?
questions.why: Hypothyroidism produces slow relaxation of deep-tendon reflexes.

questions.stem: Severe congenital hypothyroidism impairs later learning primarily through what?
questions.why: Thyroid hormones are required for early brain development and myelination.

questions.stem: Free T4 is low and TSH is greatly elevated. Which organ most likely has primary dysfunction?
questions.why: High TSH reflects attempted compensation for inadequate thyroid production.

questions.stem: Free T4 is low but TSH is inappropriately low. Which disorder best fits?
questions.why: Hypothalamic or pituitary failure leads to an inadequate TSH response.

questions.stem: Yellow skin without yellow sclerae in hypothyroidism may reflect what?
questions.why: Thyroid deficiency can impair conversion of beta-carotene to vitamin A.

questions.stem: What explains short stature with longstanding childhood hypothyroidism?
questions.why: Normal bone growth and maturation require thyroid hormone.

questions.stem: A patient has heat intolerance, tremor and raised free T4. Which TSH level suggests primary hyperthyroidism?
questions.why: Primary thyroid excess suppresses pituitary TSH by negative feedback.

questions.stem: Extracellular calcium entering a presynaptic terminal triggers which event?
questions.why: Calcium influx triggers synaptic vesicle fusion and transmitter release.

questions.stem: Why does severe hypocalcaemia cause tetany and muscle spasms?
questions.why: Low extracellular calcium lowers the threshold for spontaneous neuronal discharge.

questions.stem: Carpal spasm after inflation of a blood-pressure cuff demonstrates which sign?
questions.why: Trousseau sign is carpal spasm produced by cuff inflation.

questions.stem: Tapping the facial nerve produces twitching of facial muscles. Which sign is this?
questions.why: Chvostek sign demonstrates facial nerve hyperexcitability.

questions.stem: A hyperventilating patient develops tetany with normal total plasma calcium. What changed?
questions.why: Respiratory alkalosis increases calcium binding to albumin, lowering ionized calcium.

questions.stem: Which neurological finding is expected with significant hypercalcaemia?
questions.why: High extracellular calcium reduces neural and muscular excitability.

questions.stem: Which bone cell primarily secretes collagen-rich osteoid for mineralization?
questions.why: Osteoblasts produce the organic bone matrix.

questions.stem: Severely reduced osteoclast activity can produce which bone disorder?
questions.why: Impaired resorption causes unusually dense bone, with narrowed marrow spaces.

questions.stem: Which constituent provides most resistance to compression in healthy bone?
questions.why: Hydroxyapatite adds compressive rigidity while collagen provides tensile strength.

questions.stem: A vitamin D-deficient child has bowed legs and poor bone mineralization. Which condition is most likely?
questions.why: Rickets is defective mineralization in developing skeletal bone.

questions.stem: Which contrast best separates osteoporosis from osteomalacia?

options.label: A
options.text: Too much collagen versus low calcium

options.label: D
options.text: Less bone mass versus poor mineralization

questions.why: Osteoporosis reduces bone mass whereas osteomalacia decreases osteoid mineralization.

questions.stem: Where does the final hydroxylation yielding calcitriol mainly occur?
questions.why: Renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D to calcitriol.

questions.stem: Which endocrine signal increases the kidney's production of active vitamin D?
questions.why: PTH upregulates 1-alpha-hydroxylase during calcium deficiency.

questions.stem: Calcitriol improves calcium balance primarily through which gut effect?
questions.why: Calcitriol upregulates intestinal transport proteins to enhance calcium absorption.

questions.stem: Why can serum phosphate fall in primary hyperparathyroidism despite bone resorption?
questions.why: PTH promotes phosphate loss through the kidneys.

questions.stem: How do chief cells respond immediately when plasma ionized calcium falls?
questions.why: Low ionized calcium reduces CaSR activation and permits more PTH release.

questions.stem: Which laboratory pattern follows complete loss of parathyroid hormone secretion?
questions.why: Low PTH causes hypocalcaemia and reduced renal phosphate excretion.

questions.stem: Calcitonin lowers circulating calcium by which direct action?
questions.why: Calcitonin restrains osteoclast-mediated bone resorption.
